name: Phinehas
bio:
Phinehas was the son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron, who stepped forward at Baal Peor and speared an Israelite man and a Midianite woman engaged in idolatrous immorality, turning away the LORD's fierce wrath from the people; God rewarded him with a "covenant of peace," making him the Old Testament's foremost example of zealous priestly devotion.

When the Israelites at Shittim committed sexual immorality with Moabite women and were drawn into worshiping Baal of Peor, the LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he commanded Moses to have the leaders of the people executed in broad daylight. While Moses and the assembly wept and prayed at the entrance to the tent of meeting, an Israelite man brazenly brought a Midianite woman into his tent before everyone's eyes. Phinehas rose up from the assembly, took a spear, followed the man into the tent, and ran them both through; the plague on Israel was stopped, though twenty-four thousand had already died (Numbers 25:1-9).

The LORD said to Moses, "Phinehas... was zealous for my honor among them, so that I did not put an end to the Israelites. Therefore tell him I am making my covenant of peace with him, and it will be a covenant of a lasting priesthood for him and his descendants, because he was zealous for the honor of his God and made atonement for the Israelites" (Numbers 25:10-13). Through this decisive act of zeal, Phinehas not only saved the whole congregation from God's fierce wrath but secured for his lineage the promise of an everlasting priesthood; he later appears again in Joshua and Judges, continuing to play an important role in Israel's history.
